name: Black Hole in a Swirling Universe
convention: The mass enters as the length $m = GM/c^2$, and the rotation parameter $j$ is an inverse area. We keep factors of $c$ explicit, and the Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.

coordinates.name: Spherical

parameters.description: Mass of the hole as a length, $m = GM/c^2$; the horizon is at $r = 2m$
Rotation parameter of the swirling universe, an inverse area; at $j = 0$ the metric is Schwarzschild's

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ of Schwarzschild's chart, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\phi$ the azimuth at rest on the horizon. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{\left(r - 2m\right)\left(2j^6\,r^{13}\sin^{12}\theta - 3j^6\,r^{12}\,m\sin^{12}\theta + 4j^4\,r^9\sin^8\theta + 27j^4\,r^8\,m\sin^8\theta - 32j^4\,r^8\,m\sin^6\theta - 64j^4\,r^7\,m^2\sin^8\theta + 64j^4\,r^7\,m^2\sin^6\theta + 34j^2\,r^5\sin^4\theta - 32j^2\,r^5\sin^2\theta - 97j^2\,r^4\,m\sin^4\theta + 96j^2\,r^4\,m\sin^2\theta + 64j^2\,r^3\,m^2\sin^4\theta - 64j^2\,r^3\,m^2\sin^2\theta + m\right)}{r^3\left(1 + j^2r^4\sin^4\theta\right)^3}\dot{t}^2 + \dfrac{4j\left(r - 2m\right)\left(j^2\,r^5\sin^4\theta - 4j^2\,r^4\,m\sin^4\theta - 3r + 4m\right)\sin^2\theta\cos\theta}{\left(1 + j^2r^4\sin^4\theta\right)^3}\dot{t}\dot{\phi} + \dfrac{2j^2\,r^5\sin^4\theta - 5j^2\,r^4\,m\sin^4\theta - m}{r\left(r - 2m\right)\left(1 + j^2r^4\sin^4\theta\right)}\dot{r}^2 + \dfrac{4j^2\,r^4\sin^3\theta\cos\theta}{1 + j^2r^4\sin^4\theta}\dot{r}\dot{\theta} - \dfrac{\left(3j^2\,r^4\sin^4\theta + 1\right)\left(r - 2m\right)}{1 + j^2r^4\sin^4\theta}\dot{\theta}^2 + \dfrac{\left(2m - r\right)\left(1 - j^2r^4\sin^4\theta\right)\sin^2\theta}{\left(1 + j^2r^4\sin^4\theta\right)^3}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Cylindrical

parameters.description: Rotation parameter of the swirling universe, an inverse area; at $j = 0$ the metric is flat

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \rho, \phi, z)$ of the swirling universe with no hole, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\rho$ and $z$ lengths. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
geodesics: \ddot{\rho} + \dfrac{2j^2\,\rho\left(j^4\,\rho^{10} + 2j^2\,\rho^6 + 8j^2\,\rho^4\,z^2 + \rho^2 - 8z^2\right)}{\left(1 + j^2\rho^4\right)^3}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{8j\,\rho\,z\left(1 - j^2\rho^4\right)}{\left(1 + j^2\rho^4\right)^3}\dot{t}\dot{\phi} + \dfrac{2j^2\,\rho^3}{1 + j^2\rho^4}\dot{\rho}^2 - \dfrac{\rho\left(1 - j^2\rho^4\right)}{\left(1 + j^2\rho^4\right)^3}\dot{\phi}^2 - \dfrac{2j^2\,\rho^3}{1 + j^2\rho^4}\dot{z}^2 = 0
